items.zh: 又三洲人攝受妻妾，施設嫁娶。北拘盧洲無我所故，無攝受故，一切有情無攝受妻妾，亦無嫁娶。
items.en: Further, the people of the three continents take wives and concubines, and establish the institutions of marriage. In Uttarakuru, since there is no notion of "mine," and hence no possessive attachment, no being there takes a wife or concubine, nor is there any marriage.

items.zh: 如三洲人，如是大力鬼及欲界諸天亦爾。唯除樂化天及他化自在天。
items.en: As with the people of the three continents, so too with powerful ghosts and the desire realm's gods — with the sole exception of the Heaven of Delighting in Transformation and the Heaven of Mastery over Others' Transformations.

items.zh: 又一切欲界天眾，無有處女胎藏。然四大王眾天於父母肩上，或於懷中，如五歲小兒欻然化出；三十三天如六歲；時分天如七歲；知足天如八歲；樂化天如九歲；他化自在天如十歲。
items.en: Further, none among the desire realm's heavenly assemblies undergo pregnancy in a womb. Rather, among the Four Great Kings, a being suddenly appears, fully formed, upon its parents' shoulder or within their embrace, resembling a five-year-old child; among the Thirty-Three, resembling a six-year-old; the Time-Divisions Heaven, a seven-year-old; the Contentment Heaven, an eight-year-old; the Heaven of Delighting in Transformation, a nine-year-old; and the Heaven of Mastery over Others' Transformations, a ten-year-old.

items.title: Birth Establishment: the Three Kinds of Desire-Birth

items.zh: 復次，生建立者，謂三種欲生。或有眾生現住欲塵，由此現住欲塵故，富貴自在。彼復云何？謂一切人及四大王眾天，乃至善知足天。是名第一欲生。
items.en: Further, as for birth establishment: there are three kinds of desire-birth. There are beings who dwell directly in present desire-objects, and by reason of these present desire-objects, are wealthy, noble, and unhindered. What are these? All humans, and the Four Great Kings up through the Contentment Heaven. This is called the first desire-birth.

items.zh: 或有眾生變化欲塵，由此變化欲塵故，富貴自在。彼復云何？謂樂化天。由彼諸天為自己故，化為欲塵，非為他故；唯自變化諸欲塵故，富貴自在。是名第二欲生。
items.en: There are beings who transform desire-objects, and by reason of these transformed desire-objects, are wealthy, noble, and unhindered. What are these? The Heaven of Delighting in Transformation. Those gods transform desire-objects for their own sake, not for the sake of others; solely by transforming desire-objects for themselves are they wealthy, noble, and unhindered. This is called the second desire-birth.

items.zh: 或有眾生他化欲塵，由他所化諸欲塵故，富貴自在。彼復云何？謂他化自在天。由彼諸天為自因緣亦能變化，為他因緣亦能變化，故於自化非為希奇；用他所化欲塵為富貴自在，故說此天為他化自在。非彼諸天唯受用他所化欲塵，亦有受用自所化欲塵者。是名第三欲生。
items.en: There are beings for whom others transform desire-objects, and by reason of these desire-objects transformed by others, are wealthy, noble, and unhindered. What are these? The Heaven of Mastery over Others' Transformations. Those gods can transform objects for their own causes and conditions just as well as for others' — self-transformation holds nothing remarkable for them — and it is specifically their use of what others transform for them that constitutes their wealth, nobility, and freedom, hence this heaven is named "mastery over others' transformations." Yet it is not that these gods consume only what others transform for them; some also consume what they themselves transform. This is called the third desire-birth.

items.zh: 復有三種樂生。或有眾生用離生喜樂灌灑其身，謂初靜慮地諸天。是名第一樂生。或有眾生由定生喜樂灌灑其身，謂第二靜慮地諸天。是名第二樂生。或有眾生以離喜樂灌灑其身，謂第三靜慮地諸天。是名第三樂生。
items.en: There are, further, three kinds of joy-birth. There are beings whose entire body is, as it were, drenched in the joy and bliss born of seclusion — the gods of the first dhyāna ground. This is called the first joy-birth. There are beings whose entire body is drenched in the joy and bliss born of concentration — the gods of the second dhyāna ground. This is called the second joy-birth. There are beings whose entire body is drenched in the bliss free of joy — the gods of the third dhyāna ground. This is called the third joy-birth.

items.title: Why Establish These Six Kinds of Birth — the Three Seekings

items.zh: 問：何故建立三種欲生、三種樂生耶？答：由三種求故。一、欲求，二、有求，三、梵行求。謂若諸沙門或婆羅門墮欲求者，一切皆為三種欲生，更無增過。若諸沙門或婆羅門墮有求者，多分求樂；由貪樂故，一切皆為三種樂生。由諸世間為不苦不樂寂靜生處起追求者，極為尠少，故此以上不立為生。
items.en: Question: why establish three kinds of desire-birth and three kinds of joy-birth? Answer: because of three kinds of seeking. First, the seeking of desire; second, the seeking of existence; third, the seeking of pure conduct. Any renunciant or brahmin who falls into the seeking of desire falls entirely within these three desire-births, and reaches no further than this. Any renunciant or brahmin who falls into the seeking of existence mostly seeks bliss; because of craving for bliss, all such seeking falls entirely within these three joy-births. Because those in the world who seek out a birthplace of neither pain nor pleasure, utterly still, are extremely few, what lies above this is not established as a "birth" at all.

items.zh: 若諸沙門或婆羅門墮梵行求者，一切皆為求無漏界。或復有一墮邪梵行求者，為求不動空無邊處、識無邊處、無所有處、非想非非想處，起邪分別，謂為解脫，當知此是有上梵行求。無上梵行求者，謂求無漏界。
items.en: Any renunciant or brahmin who falls into the seeking of pure conduct seeks, in every case, the uncontaminated realm. Yet there is a further kind who falls into a mistaken seeking of pure conduct: one who seeks the unmoving fourth dhyāna, the sphere of infinite space, the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, giving rise to a mistaken judgement that this is liberation — this should be known as a seeking of pure conduct that still has something above it. The seeking of pure conduct that has nothing above it is precisely the seeking of the uncontaminated realm.

items.title: Own-Body Establishment: Four Ways a Life Can End

items.zh: 復次，自體建立者，謂於三界中所有眾生有四種得自體差別。或有所得自體，由自所害，不由他害。謂有欲界天，名遊戲忘念。彼諸天眾或時耽著種種戲樂，久相續住；由久住故，忘失憶念；由失念故，從彼處沒。或復有天，名曰意憤。彼諸天眾有時展轉角眼相視；由相視故，意憤轉增；意憤增故，從彼處沒。
items.en: Further, as for own-body establishment: among all beings throughout the three realms, there are four kinds of difference in how a body once obtained comes to an end. There are beings whose obtained body is harmed only by themselves, not by others. There is a desire-realm heaven named the Heaven of Frolic and Forgetfulness. Its host of gods, at times so given over to various kinds of play, remain absorbed in it for a long, unbroken stretch; because of this prolonged absorption, they lose mindfulness; and because mindfulness is lost, they pass away from that place. There is, further, a heaven named the Heaven of Mental Rage. Its host of gods, at times, mutually stare fixedly into one another's eyes in some exchange; because of this mutual staring, mental rage steadily intensifies; and because rage intensifies, they pass away from that place.

items.zh: 或有所得自體，由他所害，不由自害。謂處羯羅藍、遏部曇、閉尸、鍵南位，及在母腹中所有眾生。或有所得自體，亦由自害，亦由他害。謂即彼眾生處已生位，諸根圓滿，諸根成就。
items.en: There are beings whose obtained body is harmed only by others, not by themselves — namely, beings dwelling at the kalala, arbuda, peśī, and ghana stages, and all beings otherwise within the mother's womb. There are beings whose obtained body may be harmed both by themselves and by others — namely, those same beings once they have reached the already-born stage, their faculties fully formed and matured.

items.zh: 或有所得自體，亦非自害，亦非他害。謂色、無色界諸天、一切那落迦、似那落迦鬼、如來使者、住最後身、慈定、滅定、若無諍定、若處中有，如是等類。
items.en: There are beings whose obtained body is harmed neither by themselves nor by others — namely, the gods of the form and formless realms; all beings in the hells; ghosts resembling hell-beings; a Tathāgata's own messengers; those dwelling in their final body; those absorbed in loving-kindness concentration; those absorbed in cessation concentration; those absorbed in concentration free of contention; and those in the intermediate state — beings of this sort.

blocks.text: Today finishes the aspect of enjoyment and covers two more of the eight aspects of the realms: **birth** (生) and **own body** (自體). The idea of "birth" here is unusual: not physical birth, but kinds of existence that beings seek. Read with Day 31's contrast between ordinary and noble pleasure in mind.

Humans marry and give in marriage, except in **Uttarakuru**: "since there is no notion of 'mine', and hence no possessive attachment, no being there takes a wife or concubine, nor is there any marriage." Desire exists there; possession does not. (Day 29: the same people have no path.)

subs.head: How the desire gods are born

blocks.text: No god is born from a womb. Among the Four Great Kings a being "suddenly appears, fully formed, upon its parents' shoulder or within their embrace", looking like a five-year-old human child; in each higher heaven the newborn looks a year older, up to ten in the highest desire heaven. Master Cháng Bǎi explains the "Thirty-Three": eight heavens on each side of Sumeru make thirty-two, plus Indra's at the centre.
Birth is established by what beings seek. There are three **desire-births** (欲生):

items: enjoying desire-objects that are present: all humans, and the gods up to Tuṣita;
enjoying desire-objects one transforms for oneself: the gods of Delighting in Transformation;
enjoying desire-objects others transform: the gods of Mastery over Others' Transformations.

blocks.text: Master Cháng Bǎi distinguishes the two words for this power: 變 turns what exists into something else (an apple into a pear); 化 brings something forth from nothing (a peach appears).

There are three **joy-births** (樂生), the first three dhyānas, whose beings' "entire body is drenched" in the joy and bliss of seclusion, of concentration, or the bliss free of joy. Above the third dhyāna "is not established as a birth", because, as Master Cháng Bǎi explains, very few people seek a birth of neither pain nor pleasure; most want lively enjoyment of the senses or of meditative bliss.

Why establish these six births? Because of the **three seekings** (三求): seeking desire, seeking existence, and seeking pure conduct (梵行求). Pure conduct may be sought "with something above it" or "with nothing above it". Master Cháng Bǎi: those who seek the unmoving fourth dhyāna or the formless spheres, mistaking them for liberation, seek pure conduct with something above it; their pure conduct is abstinence. Those who seek the uncontaminated realm seek it with nothing above it; their pure conduct is the noble eightfold path.

subs.head: Four ways a life can be harmed

blocks.text: The seventh aspect, **own body**, classifies beings by what can end their lives:

items: harmed only by themselves, not others: two kinds of desire gods, the gods of "Frolic and Forgetfulness", who die from losing mindfulness in play, and of "Mental Rage", who die from staring at one another in mounting anger. (Master Cháng Bǎi notes that sources disagree about where these heavens are.)
harmed only by others: beings in the womb.
harmed by neither: form and formless gods, hell-beings, a Tathāgata's messengers, those in their final life, those in loving-kindness or cessation, and others.

blocks.text: Master Cháng Bǎi's story for "a Tathāgata's messengers": the doctor Jīvaka was sent by the Buddha into danger and went without fear, saying "what the Buddha says is surely right". A life under the protection of the path cannot be cut short.
The first category is the striking one: beings who die of their own heedlessness or anger. In a sense it describes all of us.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, why is there no marriage in Uttarakuru?
options: there is no notion of "mine" and no possessiveness, so no one takes a spouse and there is no marriage
quiz.why: "In Uttarakuru, since there is no notion of 'mine,' and hence no possessive attachment, no being there takes a wife or concubine, nor is there any marriage." D is wrong: desire exists, possession does not. Master Cháng Bǎi: if two are kin, the tree spirit forbids it; a newborn is laid by the road and grows by sucking a passerby's finger. The text adds that desire-realm gods marry, except in the top two heavens.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, how are desire-realm gods born?
options: no pregnancy; they suddenly appear on a parent's shoulder or lap — like a five-year-old among the Four Great Kings, rising year by year to ten in the highest desire heaven
quiz.why: "None among the desire realm's heavenly assemblies undergo pregnancy in a womb. Rather, among the Four Great Kings, a being suddenly appears, fully formed, upon its parents' shoulder or within their embrace, resembling a five-year-old child" — up to a ten-year-old in the highest desire heaven. Master Cháng Bǎi: "They are born like a five-year-old appearing suddenly, skipping infancy and gestation."

quiz.q: According to the treatise, who belongs to the first desire-birth — those enjoying present desire-objects?
options: the Heaven of Delighting in Transformation
all humans, and the Four Great Kings up through the Contentment Heaven
quiz.why: "All humans, and the Four Great Kings up through the Contentment Heaven. This is called the first desire-birth." The second is Delighting in Transformation (transforming for oneself); the third, Mastery over Others' Transformations (using what others transform). Master Cháng Bǎi: "Others transform desire-objects for them … they need not transform anything themselves — a higher grade still."

quiz.q: According to the treatise, which grounds' gods make up the three joy-births?
options: the first, second, and third dhyāna gods — drenched respectively in joy and bliss of seclusion, of concentration, and bliss free of joy
quiz.why: The text pictures each joy-birth as having its "entire body … drenched." Master Cháng Bǎi: desire's pleasure is mixed with pain; these are three truly blissful kinds of life — first-dhyāna gods, free of desire, hostility, and harm, are "as if their whole body were showered with water." Above the third, no "joy-birth" is established (see Q9-4).

quiz.q: The text distinguishes a seeking of pure conduct "with something above it" from one "with nothing above it." According to Master Cháng Bǎi, what does "pure conduct" mean in each?
options: the lesser one (seeking the unmoving fourth dhyāna and formless spheres, mistaking them for liberation) practices abstinence from sex; the unsurpassed one (seeking the uncontaminated realm) practises the noble eightfold path
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Those who fall into mistaken pure-conduct seeking have a seeking with something above it; their pure conduct is abstaining from sex"; "those who seek the uncontaminated realm have the unsurpassed seeking; their pure conduct is the noble eightfold path." He also relays Venerable Miào Jìng's view that "unmoving" should be read together with the formless spheres. (The reading note adds a story about Udraka Rāmaputra, "Devadatta's uncle," and a flying fox; nothing of the kind appears in the lecture — logged in the correction list.)

quiz.q: According to the treatise, whose body is harmed only by themselves, not by others?
options: the desire-realm Heavens of Frolic and Forgetfulness and of Mental Rage
quiz.why: The Frolic gods, "so given over to various kinds of play … lose mindfulness; and because mindfulness is lost, they pass away"; the Rage gods "stare fixedly into one another's eyes … because rage intensifies, they pass away." Master Cháng Bǎi: "One kind dies of pleasure, the other of anger." B is harm by others; C and D are harm by neither.

quiz.q: The text lists beings harmed neither by themselves nor by others. Which is NOT on the list?
quiz.why: The list: form and formless gods, all hell-beings, ghosts resembling hell-beings, a Tathāgata's messengers, those in their final body, those in loving-kindness, cessation, or non-contention concentration, and those in the intermediate state. The Wheel-Turning King is not listed. Master Cháng Bǎi: before entering cessation one can resolve that water, fire, and poison shall not harm one.
